newsitem.title: USA: Clinton readying State of the Union speech.
newsitem.headline: Clinton readying State of the Union speech.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was to report to Congress and the country on Tuesday that the State of the Union is sound, and, in a high-profile speech, lay out his plan for maintaining peace and prosperity.
"Education will be the focus. The president will have a detailed agenda for bringing America's schools up to world class standards," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

Clinton was to deliver the televised State of the Union speech, giving a broad overview of where the United States stands and where he wants to take it, at 9 p.m. EST on Tuesday (0200 GMT on Wednesday).

"Usually democracies get lazy in times of peace and prosperity. The changes and challenges of this time do not permit us to do this. If we do it, we will regret it for a very long time," Clinton told Democratic governors on Monday.

McCurry said the Democratic president, who began a second four-year term on Jan. 20, would propose new initiatives to expand health care coverage for millions of children, fight juvenile crime and rid U.S. schools of illicit drugs.
A recent study found that about 10 million American kids, or almost 15 percent, have no health insurance and many of them are not enrolled in the Medicaid health care programme for the poor.

Clinton also planned to use the speech to talk about how to carry out a new welfare law that ends a 61-year guarantee of federal aid to the poor and to try to take the steam out of a Republican drive for a Constitutional amendment requiring a balanced budget.

"The president will certainly talk about the importance of balancing the budget and talk about his budget plan to do it, and he'll suggest that we ought to do it and get on with that business," McCurry said.
He added that Clinton would tell the country that a budget amendment "is a moot question" if Congress and the president get together and balance the budget by a certain date.

Clinton's report is mandated by the Constitution, which says the president "shall from time to time give to the Congress information of the State of the Union, and recommend to their consideration such measures as he shall judge necessary and expedient."
A Republican response was to be delivered by Representative J.C. Watts of Oklahoma, a black former collegiate football standout who is one of the rising stars of the opposition party.

One sidelight of Clinton's speech, which was to take place in the chamber of the House of Representatives -- the traditional forum for this presidential oration -- was the planned absence of Agricuture Secretary Dan Glickman.

Glickman, according to a White House official who did not wish to be identified, is the designated survivor for the speech, taking his turn in a macabre rotation that ensures that someone in the national leadership will be left to carry on if all those at the Capitol for the speech are somehow wiped out.

The practice of designating one member of the president's Cabinet to stay away from an occasion of state as a national security precaution dates from the darkest days of the Cold War, when it was feared a gathering of the nation's leaders might present a tempting target for a surprise nuclear attack.
Decapitation, the doomsday term for eliminating a nation's leadership structure, remains a threat because of terrorism.
